questions: Did slalom progress rise above 0.34, and did line_loss_events on the slalom fall from 0.35 toward 0?
Did the narrower 0.08 m track reduce off-track ends on the s-bend and oval, or did max_error still reach 0.06 m?
Did steering_oscillation rise sharply (for example above 0.5 on the s-bend) compared with iteration 3's 0.44, indicating the sharper turn response is overshooting?
If the slalom still ends off track with line loss near zero, is the sensor reach at +/-0.06 m now too short, so the next step should be +/-0.07 m?

intent: Test whether turn authority is now the limit on the slalom and the remaining oval and s-bend off-track ends. Changes from iteration 3: wheel_track narrowed from 0.10 m to 0.08 m to raise turn rate per unit of controller command. Sensor array (7 sensors at x = +/-0.06 m, y = 0.05 m, 16 mm footprints), mass (0.6 kg), body (0.12 x 0.10 m) and wheel radius (0.03 m) are unchanged, so the effect of the track change can be read alone. Expected result: slalom progress above 0.34 with fewer off-track ends and possibly a first finish, oval finish rate at or above 0.85, and s-bend max_error at or below 0.06 m.
learning: Iteration 3 showed that the s-bend failure came from turn response and lead, not sensing: restoring the 0.05 m lead and lowering yaw inertia lifted s-bend progress from 0.04 to 0.75. The slalom is now the binding track, with line loss and max_error just over the off-track limit. The next test separates turn authority from the rest by changing only wheel_track. If the slalom still loses the line, the next lever is outer-sensor reach, not the controller.
rationale: Iteration 3 is the first clear improvement: score 493.2 from 39.5, with s-bend progress 0.75 (from 0.04) and oval finish rate 0.85. The change that drove this was restoring the 0.05 m lead and cutting yaw inertia through mass 0.6 kg and body 0.12 x 0.10 m. The two were applied together, so the split between them is unknown. Line loss on the s-bend is 0 and the oval is 0.25 per run, so the 7-sensor reach at +/-0.06 m is working. The remaining failure is the slalom, which finishes 0 of 20 with progress 0.34, line loss 0.35 and max_error 0.0624 (just above the 0.06 m off-track limit). The oval and s-bend still have off-track ends (3 and 14 of 20), and the s-bend max_error is 0.060. The Integrator's rule for this case applies: line loss is 0 on the s-bend and progress is well above 0.25, so the geometry is kept and the next lever is turn authority. Body width cannot help, because the off-track limit is max(0.06, 0.0125 + body_width/4) and stays at 0.06 for any body under 0.19 m. I therefore narrow wheel_track from 0.10 to 0.08 m. Turn rate is the wheel speed difference divided by track, so the same controller command produces a sharper turn, which targets the slalom's tight alternating bends. Everything else is held (lead 0.05 m, 7 sensors at +/-0.06 m, 16 mm footprints, mass 0.6 kg, body 0.12 x 0.10 m), so this iteration isolates turn authority. Expected result: slalom progress rises clearly above 0.34 with fewer off-track ends, and oval and s-bend finish rates hold or improve. Main risk: the sharper turn response may raise steering_oscillation, which is already 0.44 on the s-bend.
